svg.text: One Django 5 project (MTV monolith + Django REST Framework). Business features are split into apps — accounts, catalog, cart, orders, payments, notifications — over Postgres, with Redis cache + Celery for background work. Representative canonical layout.

svg.text: Canonical Django layout: a config package + one app per feature. Colours match the app columns & runtime nodes.
Each app is a small MTV + DRF stack
services.py → business logic (kept out of views)
Prod: gunicorn config.wsgi + celery -A config worker
2 · Apps as columns — each is a URL → View → Serializer → Service → Model stack
One shared request pipeline (server + middleware + router) fans out to every app's DRF view. All models live in one Postgres database.
Middleware chain (runs on every request, reversed on the response)
AuthenticationMiddleware · MessageMiddleware · (+ DRF auth / throttling in the view)
matches the URL and dispatches to the right View
business logic kept out of the view
PostgreSQL — ONE database shared by every app (the ORM maps each app's models to tables)
auth_user · accounts_address · catalog_product / category · cart_cart / cartitem · orders_order / orderitem · payments_payment — kept consistent by migrations
URL match → dispatch to the matching ViewSet
3 · Runtime — one deployment: Nginx → Gunicorn/Django → Postgres, with Redis cache + Celery workers

Read it as: ① browser hits Nginx over HTTPS → ② Nginx proxies dynamic requests to a Gunicorn worker running Django (and serves static/media itself) → ③ the view/service reads & writes Postgres via the ORM

→ ④ Django caches in Redis and enqueues background tasks → ⑤ Celery workers pull tasks from Redis → ⑥ and call email/SMS providers. The payment gateway is called synchronously during checkout. One deployable, scaled by adding Gunicorn + Celery processes.

g.text: POST /api/orders (Bearer JWT) → Nginx → Gunicorn → Django middleware (security, session, auth sets request.user).
Router dispatches to OrderViewSet.create(); DRF runs authentication + permissions + throttling.
CheckoutSerializer validates the body (address, payment method) — returns 400 on bad input.
Service reads the cart (CartService), checks stock (CatalogService) and decrements it (row locks).
Calls PaymentService.charge() → payment gateway (HTTPS). If it fails, the whole transaction rolls back.
Creates Order + OrderItems (price snapshot), clears the cart, then commits the transaction.
An order_placed signal enqueues a Celery task → notifications.send_email (async, off the request thread).
OrderSerializer renders the body; DRF returns 201 Created; Nginx passes it back to the client.

svg.text: # 400 on invalid body · 402/409 if payment or stock fails (tx rolled back)
# email is sent later by Celery — the response does NOT wait for it
• Steps 5–7 run in one DB transaction — stock, payment record and order
commit together or not at all (no half-placed orders).
• The payment webhook (async) later confirms/settles and updates status,
• Slow work (email, receipts) is pushed to Celery so the API stays fast.
• The same views/services back the Django admin and any server-rendered
Self-contained SVG · viewBox 3400×2560 (rendered 6800×5120) · app-coloured across the project tree, layer view & runtime. Representative Django 5 + DRF e-commerce layout.
